findings.title: SDK result usage reader assumes the untyped usage object is a mapping
findings.description: `read_result_usage()` documents `msg.usage` as an untyped CLI value read defensively, but after the `None` check it only type-annotates `usage: dict[str, Any] = msg.usage`; there is no runtime mapping check. `_usage_int()` at `src/squadron/providers/sdk/usage.py:57-62` then does `key not in usage` and `usage[key]`, which raises `TypeError` for a non-mapping such as a list or int. `tests/providers/sdk/test_usage.py` covers `usage=None` and malformed fields, but not a malformed `usage` object. A single bad SDK result can crash the session/review path before provider-error telemetry is attached. Guard with `isinstance(msg.usage, Mapping)`, warn once, and return `(None, turns, cost)`; add a regression test.

findings.title: Boolean usage metadata can be persisted as an unreadable record
findings.description: `record_from_message()` accepts `turns if isinstance(turns, int)` and `cost if isinstance(cost, float | int)`. Because `bool` subclasses `int`, metadata containing `True`/`False` is accepted, then `UsageRecord.to_dict()` writes booleans into run state. `UsageRecord.from_dict()` in `src/squadron/core/usage.py` rejects bool via `_opt_int()`, so `sq stats run` later marks that row unreadable. Other boundaries explicitly exclude booleans (`src/squadron/providers/sdk/usage.py:68-72`, `src/squadron/stats/reviews_report.py:130-135`), so this is inconsistent boundary validation. Exclude `bool` here and add a test that malformed provider metadata produces `None` fields rather than a corrupt persisted record.

findings.title: Failed compact actions discard provider-error telemetry
findings.description: `CompactAction._execute_sdk_rotate()` now measures `started` and requires a `UsageCapture`, and its success path stamps the reply telemetry. Its broad `except Exception` around `context.sdk_session.compact()` returns a failed `ActionResult` with no metadata and never calls `record_from_error()` or `record_from_telemetry()`. `SDKExecutionSession.dispatch()` attaches partial telemetry to `ProviderError` on failure, and dispatch/review/summary paths record that spend; compact does not. This violates the new failure-mode expectation that a failed I/O/LLM call has an observable usage signal. Add a `ProviderError` branch that stamps available telemetry (including partial on unusable stalls) and a test with a stalled compact call.

findings.title: `sq stats reviews --json` emits plain text on stdout when the reviews directory is missing
findings.description: `stats_reviews()` computes `reviews_dir`, calls `reviews_usage_report()`, and on `report.missing_dir` calls `typer.echo("No review directory at ...")` before reaching the `as_json` branch. With `--json`, stdout therefore contains human text instead of parseable JSON, while the command still exits 0. `commands/sq/stats.md` and `commands/agents/sq-stats/SKILL.md` both advertise `--json` for `reviews`. `tests/cli/test_stats.py` only covers the missing-directory table path, not `--json`. Emit the same empty report shape as JSON (with `missing_dir`), or write the message to stderr and exit non-zero; add a `--json` regression test.

findings.title: `sq stats reviews` does not use the project’s shared review-directory resolution
findings.description: The new command hard-codes `Path.cwd() / REVIEWS_DIR`. Review/runtime paths use `resolve_repo_cwd()` in `src/squadron/cli/commands/review.py:286-292` to anchor at the git root, and `resolve_reviews_dir()` in `src/squadron/review/reviews_dir.py#resolve_reviews_dir` handles config/PR external review directories. Running `sq stats reviews` from a repository subdirectory with no `--cwd`/`--reviews-dir` reports “No review directory” even when the repo-root reviews exist; PR reviews saved to an external directory are never visible to stats. The CLI tests monkeypatch into a temp root and create the expected directory there, so they do not cover this path drift. Route through the shared resolution (or expose equivalent flags) and test from a nested directory plus an external reviews directory.

findings.title: `reviews_usage_report()` counts any frontmattered markdown as a review
findings.description: The loop globs `*.md`, parses frontmatter, applies the slice filter, and excludes `runId`; it never checks `docType: review` or `reviewType`. Any markdown file in the reviews directory with a YAML mapping therefore becomes a `ReviewUsageRow` and contributes to `UsageTotals`. The test fixtures hard-code `docType: review` in `tests/stats/test_reviews_report.py:12-18`, but the production code ignores that key and no test covers a non-review document in the same directory. Filter on the persisted review contract (at minimum `docType == "review"`) before building a row, and add a negative test.

findings.title: Unreadable review artifacts can abort the whole stats report
findings.description: `read_frontmatter()` in `src/squadron/documents/frontmatter.py:59-70` calls `Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`; it returns `None` for missing/invalid YAML blocks, but `OSError`, `UnicodeDecodeError`, and a file removed after `glob()` propagate. `reviews_usage_report()` only handles `front is None`, so one permission error or invalid UTF-8 artifact crashes `sq stats reviews` with a traceback instead of incrementing `skipped`. The report’s `skipped` field is documented as “unreadable frontmatter”, and the new tests only exercise a text file with no fence. Catch specific read/decode errors, log a WARNING naming the path, increment `skipped`, and continue; add a test for an unreadable/invalid-encoding artifact.

findings.title: Standalone review reports cannot recover the alias from `requestedModel`
findings.description: `_record()` sets `alias=requested if requested in get_all_aliases() else None`, reading `requestedModel`. Persistence writes `requestedModel` only when `result.model_substituted` is true and writes the resolved model id (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py:459`); `run_review_with_profile()` sets `result.requested_model = resolved_model` after alias resolution. It does not write the alias name, and normal reviews omit the key entirely. As a result, standalone review `UsageRecord.alias` is almost always `None`; `cost_cell()` in `src/squadron/cli/stats_views.py:166-179` cannot identify `cost_tier = "subscription"` aliases, so provider costs are rendered as real money (`$0.41 prov`) instead of `api-rate equiv.`. `tests/stats/test_reviews_report.py` hand-writes `requestedModel="opus"`, which production frontmatter does not produce. Persist the resolved alias explicitly (for example `aiAlias`) and read that key in the stats report, with a test using a real formatted review artifact.

structured_findings.summary: SDK result usage reader assumes the untyped usage object is a mapping
Boolean usage metadata can be persisted as an unreadable record
Failed compact actions discard provider-error telemetry
`sq stats reviews --json` emits plain text on stdout when the reviews directory is missing
`sq stats reviews` does not use the project’s shared review-directory resolution
`reviews_usage_report()` counts any frontmattered markdown as a review
Unreadable review artifacts can abort the whole stats report
Standalone review reports cannot recover the alias from `requestedModel`
